identity.title: Stochastic Modeling of the Time Variability of ALMA Calibrators
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific

paper_type_evidence.quote: we model the variability of 39 quasars which have been used by ALMA as secondary flux calibrators using continuous time stochastic processes.

question.value: Can mixtures of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes describe the multi-frequency flux and spectral index variability of ALMA grid calibrators, and provide forecasts, interpolations and uncertainties?

evidence.quote: We find that simple mixtures of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes can describe well the flux and spectral index variability of these sources for Bands 3 and 7

bands.value: Band 3 and 7 (mostly 91.5, 103.5 and 343.5 GHz), some Band 6

evidence.quote: mostly at 91.5 and 103.5 GHz, and at 343.5 GHz, respectively.
from Cycle 5 on, observations for the calibrator survey are performed using the Morita ALMA compact array (ACA) and the ACA correlators.
On-source time spent on each grid calibrator varies between 2–4 minutes.

provided.value: Additional calibrator measurements, including Bands 8-10, used for J2253+1608

evidence.loc: Combining calibrator survey with additional data
evidence.quote: Additional measurements for many calibrators are provided by the ALMACAL survey

what.value: Grid calibrator list (Table 10.1 of the ALMA Technical Handbook) and public calibrator source catalogue flux densities

evidence.quote: The list of secondary flux calibrators known as the grid sources is given by Table 10.1 from .

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: 100 simulated OU-1F1a light-curves (400 measurements each, 1080 d) used to test MLE recovery

evidence.quote: we generate 100 OU-1F1a simulated light-curves at 91.5, 103.5, and 343.5 GHz

archive_products_used_as_is.value: Flux densities taken from the public ALMA calibrator source catalogue

evidence.loc: Combining calibrator survey with additional data
evidence.quote: The flux densities used in the light-curves analyzed in this work come from data taken by the calibration survey and reported in the source catalog.

what.value: Data reduction of grid calibrator survey and OU mixture formalism follow earlier works

evidence.quote: More details about the design, observational strategy, and data reduction procedure of the grid calibrator survey can be found in .

unstated_but_needed: Exact catalogue download date and version, and the 20 masked outlier points (only in supplementary text file)
Metropolis-Hastings chain length and step size
Selection criteria for the best model per source beyond heuristic judgement

analysis_steps.goal: Fit simple spectral model and compute variability index

method.value: Least-squares fit of power law to all data per source at nu0=100 GHz; vix computed

evidence.quote: we obtain least squared fitted parameters to all the data available for each calibrator, disregarding its variability.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit OU-mixture models by maximum likelihood

method.value: State space representation with Kalman recursions to compute likelihood; MLE of OU-rFsa models with optional curvature and nu-lag

evidence.loc: Determination of the best-fit stochastic model
evidence.quote: To calculate the likelihood function we use the state space representation of each process together with the Kalman recursions

key_parameters.value: r<=2, s<=1; sigma_N proportional to nu^1/2

evidence.quote: In practice, for this work we use $r\le2$ and $s\le1$ models.

fitting.value: Likelihood maximization with Minuit; parabolic uncertainties from Hessian

evidence.loc: Determination of the best-fit stochastic model
evidence.quote: We use the `Minuit` (cite: JAMES1975343) package implemented within `PDL`[^2] to obtain the MLE and their uncertainties.

validation.value: AIC, normalized residuals, Anderson-Darling test, ACF, Ljung-Box; recovery on 100 simulated light-curves

evidence.quote: We test the normality of the residuals running the Anderson-Darling test

method.value: Kalman forecasts with stochastic plus parametric uncertainty added in quadrature; compared against next measurements, a Metropolis-Hastings posterior and the P0 interpolation

evidence.quote: we calculate the total uncertainty on the forecast as the sum in quadrature of the parametric and stochastic uncertainties.

fitting.value: Metropolis-Hastings MCMC with constant prior starting from MLE

evidence.quote: We sample the posterior using a Metropolis-Hastings Markov chain (cite: gregory2005bayesian) starting from the MLE

validation.value: Standardized forecast differences against subsequent measurements (56 Band 3, 41 Band 7)

evidence.quote: For the full grid sample, there are 56 and 41 of these measurements in total for Bands 3 and 7, respectively.
R (v. 3.5.0) computer programs to generate the simulated datasets

evidence.loc: Determination of the best-fit stochastic model
evidence.quote: We use the `Minuit` (cite: JAMES1975343) package implemented within `PDL`[^2] to obtain the MLE and their uncertainties.
PDL code implementing the Kalman recursions (Appendix A) is given in the supplementary material
using the `ad.test` task from package `goftest`

results_numeric.quantity: Stochastic model interpolation scatter vs P0 for J0635-7516, Band 3

evidence.loc: Flux interpolation: comparison between two methods
evidence.quote: For P0, the standard deviation of the differences at Bands 3 and 7 are 7% and 11%, respectively

results_numeric.quantity: Spectral indices of 32 of 39 sources range

evidence.quote: with 32 out of 39 spectral indices between $-0.35$ and $-0.80$
Five sources are apparently characterized by a significant frequency dependent lag between their Band 3 and 7 light-curves.

findings_qualitative.value: Spectral-index OU term and concavity substantially improve fits over single OU with constant index

evidence.quote: We see that the addition of stochastic time-variability to the spectral index (a $\beta$ term) accounts for a significant diminishing in the AIC ($\sim420$).

claims.hypothesis: Can OU mixtures model calibrator multi-frequency variability?
claims.experiment: MLE fits to 39 grid calibrators in Bands 3 and 7 with residual diagnostics
claims.result: Selected models include spectral-index variation for 38 sources; residuals near white noise
claims.finding: OU mixtures describe the variability well

evidence.quote: most (38) sources are better modeled with an additional OU-process describing the spectral index variations.

claims.hypothesis: Does stochastic interpolation beat the pipeline-like P0 method?
claims.experiment: Leave-one-day-out interpolation for J0635-7516 and phase calibrators
claims.result: Lower scatter for stochastic model (3%/5% vs 7%/11%); lower median in 26 of 40 cases

evidence.loc: Application to less frequently sampled data: phase calibrators
evidence.quote: in the majority of the cases (26 of 40, among all Bands and sources) the median of the absolute differences is lower for the stochastic estimations.

limitations_admitted.value: Decorrelation time poorly constrained because monitoring baseline is short

evidence.quote: Specifically, the decorrelation time — which is defining of the OU-process — cannot be recovered.

referee_caveats_inferred: Calibrator fluxes depend on SSO calibration, correlated errors not modelled
Model selection per source is heuristic

evidence.quote: Flux densities, positions, and calibrator type can be obtained from the online source catalogue.

code_released.value: PDL Kalman code in supplementary material and ASCL; R scripts for simulations

evidence.quote: can also be obtained from the Astrophysics Source Code Library

reproducibility.score_reason: Public catalogue, code released, clear equations; some details only in supplement.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public catalogue data, complete recipe, numeric tables of fit parameters.

now_not_stated.old_value: Gaussian stationary stochastic process in log-flux; fiducial frequency 100 GHz
